Technical & price structure: In plain terms: Al Rajhi Bank trades a few percent below our weighted central fair value — roughly fairly valued, and the whole argument is what its retained capital is worth. On the dividend it pays today (a rising ~half of earnings) the shares look fairly priced near SAR 58; on the value it builds by reinvesting at a ~23% return, the excess-return lenses land at SAR 76–80. It is the world's largest Islamic bank — a retail-led franchise with the Kingdom's deepest low-cost deposit base, earning ~23% on equity at a sector-low ~23% cost-to-income. The bull case (~SAR 80) is durable margin resilience and a step-up to a 55–60% payout; the cautious case (~SAR 58) is a faster SAMA cutting cycle that squeezes the net interest margin and incremental capital earning closer to the cost of equity. What moves it near-term is the rate path and the quarterly NIM print.
